transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-04-27
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Maya Ortiz (RiverMark - Head of ML); Liam Murphy (RiverMark - Platform Eng); Sanjay Rao (RiverMark - SRE)

Auto-generated Summary: Weekly POC check-in for latency tuning. Focused on TTFT, streaming degradation at long sequences, and kernel/quantization experiments.

00:00 Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, quick check that audio's good?
00:08 Maya Ortiz: yep, can hear you, faint echo but it's fine.
00:15 Samir Patel: cool, i'll share the deck after, but today i want to focus on TTFT numbers and a kernel sweep plan
01:02 Liam Murphy: before we start, remind us the current numbers we saw last week for p50 and p95 on the hosted endpoints?
01:18 Avery Chen: sure, p50 about 120ms for short seqs, p95 around 420ms; for long sequences (>1024) p95 jumps to ~1.2s, TTFT was around 90-110ms depending on model and batch
02:05 Maya Ortiz: that p95 is the thing for our UI charts — customers see the spikes. we're trying to keep first token under 200ms most of the time
02:40 Samir Patel: right, so two levers: kernel selection / quantization and streaming behavior. streaming currently chunks at 64 tokens, that adds a small delay before first chunk for longer generations
03:15 Sanjay Rao: also our seq distribution is skewed; median is 64 but tail at 1500 for a subset of requests; we can provide histogram
03:45 Avery Chen: perfect, send that histogram, that'll help Samir pick the kernel profile that matches your workload
04:10 Samir Patel: quick note — TTFT can be improved by forcing earlier flushes and smaller first chunk sizes, but that trades off throughput; we'll test 8/16/32 token first-chunk sizes
04:55 Maya Ortiz: what's the impact on cost? smaller chunks means more network overhead, right?
05:12 Samir Patel: yeah slight increase; Redwood Optimize recommendations estimate ~3-7% overhead for 8-token first chunk on your traffic mix, but p95 TTFT drops substantially in many cases
05:45 Liam Murphy: can you explain the kernel sweep? are we talking CUDA kernels + attention optimizations or also quantization?
06:02 Samir Patel: both; we'll test kernel families (default cuda kernel set A vs kernel set B with fused attention) plus quantization flavors: FP16, INT8/8-bit, and mixed 16/8 profiles. also check KV cache handling for streaming to avoid repeated recompute
06:40 Maya Ortiz: any risk of quality regression with INT8? we've seen hallucination increase in earlier tests
06:55 Samir Patel: good call — quality needs to be checked. we'll run a small eval set — your 100 prompts we used earlier — and report perplexity/delta and qualitative failures alongside latency
07:22 Sanjay Rao: networking wise, we need to confirm VPC egress and KMS for keys before we flip to Dedicated. last time there was a question about outbound IP ranges
07:40 Avery Chen: understood — SRE deep-dive next week can cover VPC egress, egress IPs, and KMS integration. i'll own scheduling
08:05 Maya Ortiz: also about fallback: if Dedicated capacity is constrained, do you have automatic fallback to hosted model variants? we need predictable behavior for spikes
08:22 Samir Patel: yes — smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants in hosted pool; we can set cost vs latency policies. we'll document the exact fallback chain for your pilot
09:00 Liam Murphy: curious about batching. does Redwood do dynamic batching on Dedicated? our goal is low latency at low QPS, not high throughput
09:18 Samir Patel: yes dynamic continuous batching with latency SLOs. for low QPS we favor immediate dispatch with minimal batching; we can configure batching thresholds per route
09:45 Maya Ortiz: can you quantify TTFT improvement if we switch to the fused attention kernel? ballpark numbers?
10:05 Samir Patel: from similar workloads, fused attention + FP16 gave ~15-25% TTFT reduction on models in your size range; INT8 can push further but quality checks required. exact numbers depend on sequence length and KV caching
10:40 Avery Chen: Samir, can you run an experiment: baseline (current hosted config), fused-attn FP16, fused-attn INT8 with KV caching enabled, and streaming first-chunk sizes 8/16/32. include p50/p95 TTFT, overall throughput, and token cost estimates
11:05 Samir Patel: noted. i'll produce a CSV with per-config per-seq-length rows. expects to take 3-4 days to collect stable stats
11:25 Maya Ortiz: okay, timeline's fine as long as we see numbers before the pilot gating review 5/12
11:40 Sanjay Rao: quick question on monitoring — can we get token-level traces and per-request latency breakdown in Console? we need to slice by route and model version
11:58 Avery Chen: yes, Console provides token & route breakdowns; we can add tracing hooks. we'll also export a sample trace to you for validation
12:20 Liam Murphy: about the sample traffic — we'll anonymize and upload to the shared drive. expect a 1k request set with seq histogram by Friday
12:40 Maya Ortiz: also want to test streaming vs non-streaming UX; maybe Samir can include both endpoints in the sweep
12:55 Samir Patel: will include streaming and immediate (blocking) generation; note that blocking gives lower total latency for some mid-size seq but loses streaming UX benefits
13:30 Avery Chen: competitive note — you mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI earlier; our approach is to measure TTFT across kernels rather than rely on a single provider; we'll include competitor baselines if you want but might add noise unless you have identical prompts run there
14:00 Maya Ortiz: not necessary now, maybe later for procurement comparisons
14:20 Sanjay Rao: network ask: we'll need explicit egress IPs and a small change window for firewall rules. can you provide a list?
14:35 Avery Chen: yes, we'll get standard egress ranges and a template change window. Samir, add that to the deliverables?
14:48 Samir Patel: added
15:05 Avery Chen: quick recap then next steps — Samir will run kernel/quant sweep and share spreadsheet by 5/4; RiverMark to upload sample traffic by 4/30; Avery to send pricing and schedule SRE deep-dive week of 5/10; SREs to confirm KMS/ip constraints by 5/7
15:35 Maya Ortiz: good recap, thanks all
15:45 Liam Murphy: any blockers from our side? none at the moment
15:55 Sanjay Rao: none, thanks
16:05 Avery Chen: ok we'll follow up with the links now
16:10 Samir Patel: sharing interim spreadsheet link and deck in chat (link: https://redwood.example.com/s/latency-sweeps-rivermark)
16:25 Avery Chen: security doc link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/security/rivermark-soc2-kms (note: internal SSO required)
